indicators.indicator_description: Rewrite numerical and algebraic expressions of irrational and rational numbers involving radicals, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division (limited to square and cube roots).
constraints: Limited to square and cube roots

indicators.indicator_description: Translate between rational exponents and radical expressions of irrational and rational numbers. Use properties of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division to simplify radical and rational expressions (limited to square and cube roots).
constraints: Limited to square and cube roots

standard_title: Equations and Expressions in One Variable

indicators.indicator_description: Transform an equation in one variable to create new equations that have the same solution as the original and justify the steps taken.
Solve literal equations and formulas for a specified variable including equations and formulas that arise in a variety of disciplines.
Solve mathematical and real-world situations using linear, quadratic, exponential (same bases), and linear absolute value equations in one variable.
constraints: Limited to linear, quadratic, exponential (same bases), and linear absolute value equations in one variable

indicators.indicator_description: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials with initial terms up to a degree of 2.
constraints: Initial terms up to a degree of 2

standard_title: Equations and Inequalities in Two or More Variables

indicators.indicator_description: Transform linear, quadratic, exponential, and linear absolute value functions to equivalent forms to identify slope and y-intercept for linear, vertex, and roots (if any) for quadratic and linear absolute value, and y-intercept for exponential.
constraints: Limited to linear, quadratic, exponential, and linear absolute value functions

indicators.indicator_description: Solve systems of linear equations algebraically and graphically.
Solve real-world and mathematical situations using linear and exponential inequalities in two variables.
constraints: Limited to linear and exponential inequalities in two variables

indicators.indicator_description: Create, solve, and graph linear inequalities in two variables.
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.
Create symbolic representations of linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given graphs, verbal descriptions, and tables.
constraints: Limited to linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences

indicators.indicator_description: Use graphs to obtain exact and/or approximate solutions of equations, inequalities, and systems of linear equations in two variables (given or obtained by using technology).
Solve an equation of the form f(x) = g(x) graphically by identifying the x-coordinate(s) of the point(s) of intersection of the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x).

standard_title: Represent and Interpret Functions Symbolically and Graphically

indicators.indicator_description: Recognize that f(x) denotes the output of function f that corresponds to the input x, and this corresponds to the set of all the ordered pairs (x, y) that satisfy the equation y = f(x) both tabularly and graphically.

Use the definition of a function to analyze the domain and range of a function in relation to its graph, mapping, table, verbal, and/or symbolic description and, where applicable, using interval and set notation.

Translate among graphical, tabular, verbal, and symbolic representations in function notation, to identify intercepts, intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, constant, maximums and minimums, and symmetries and explain their meanings in real-world and mathematical situations.

Describe the effect of the transformations kf(x), f(x) + k, f(x - k), and combinations of such transformations on the graph of parent function y = f(x) for any real number k; find the value of k given the graphs; and write the equation of a transformed parent function given its graph.
Given a real-world or mathematical situation, determine the parent graph that best models the situation.

Given different representations of two different functions, compare key features including intercepts, domain and range, intervals of increasing and decreasing, constant, average rate of change, and maximum and minimum values.

standard_title: Summarize, Represent, and Interpret Data on Two Variables

indicators.indicator_description: Summarize categorical data in two-way frequency tables, interpret relative frequencies in real-world situations, and informally determine possible associations and trends in the data.
Summarize quantitative data in a table and on a scatterplot and describe how the variables are associated (limit to linear data).
Find a linear function for a scatterplot that suggests a linear association.
For linear associations, use technology to determine the correlation coefficient, evaluate the strength of the association, and find the line of best fit.

standard_title: Analyze and Interpret Models for Two Variables

indicators.indicator_description: Use two-way frequency tables to make inferences and interpret the data in terms of real-world or mathematical situations.
Interpret the slope and the intercept of a linear model in the context of the data.
Use a linear model to interpolate and extrapolate unknown values close to the data set.
Identify any limitations specific to a real-world situation.
